title: Volume 1 Chapter 3: Fallen Fairies
content: NOTE: If you read chapter 1 & 2, you should re-read it, there was a problem with the translation file making both chapter incomplete.
Leading the way down the corridor of the academy building, Louise turned around and began proudly explaining the facilities while walking backward.
"The academy was originally built as a floating fortress in the sky. Before we knew it, the facility for training Valkyries grew larger, and it became known as the academy."
The fortress that operated the Valkyries, currently the most effective against Gijuu, had always been highly secretive.
In the days of infantry, its existence was rumored, but no one believed it was real.
A fortress that nurtured and operated Valkyries... If a comic book artist heard this, they would surely be thrilled to turn it into a manga.
While I was reminiscing about my comrades, Louise continued to explain the facility.
"This is the library. There are quite a few rare books, but due to the preferences of the library committee, some strange books have also been purchased, so it’s worth checking out."
"Strange books, you say?"
"Not too long ago, there were a lot of urban legend types. Recently, it's more about historical ones."
For just a brief moment, Louise cast a melancholic glance at the entrance of the library.
She quickly switched her expression and began talking about the next facility before we even arrived.
"Next is the break room. However, there are places that Class Five students can’t use. Only official Valkyries can access those areas, so just remember that they’re off-limits."
I thought it wouldn’t be a problem if I researched the facilities in advance, but it was significant to grasp the academy's formal or informal rules.
I had assumed that I wouldn’t be using most of the facilities anyway.
However, the academy was different from the military bases I had been in before.
If I wasn’t careful, I might have unknowingly broken their rules and made someone uncomfortable.
Thanks to Louise, I was able to learn this in advance, which I appreciated.
"Accepting Louise’s proposal was the right choice. I was still thinking of the academy as just another typical military base, so I would have caused problems if I hadn’t known anything."
"Really? I’m glad if I could be of help to you, Ren-kun!"
Louise, smiling brightly, seemed genuinely happy.
"Now for today’s main event! I’ll show you my favorite place, Ren-kun!"
"Your favorite place? Is that why we’re heading underground?"
What lay ahead as we exited the school building was an entrance that seemed to lead down to the basement.
The entrance to the stairs leading to the basement, which looked like a small storage room, had a slightly rusted shutter that was closed but didn’t seem to be locked.
There were no signs indicating it was off-limits, so it was likely a place we could enter without issue.
As I observed carefully, it seemed Louise noticed my caution.
"The underground of a fortress floating in the sky is a strange story, isn’t it? But you don’t have to worry. There’s a storage area down below where various tools are kept."
"I’m not worried. I just didn’t expect you to be interested in the basement, Louise."
Since Louise was acting so cheerful, I had unconsciously formed the impression that she preferred bright places.
Louise tilted her head.
"Really? But the lower levels are like a maze, so exploring them is fun!"
"A maze, you say?"
"The academy has been expanded continuously, but it seems it was easier to extend vertically than horizontally. Because of that, unused facilities seem to have gotten buried."
I was convinced that this was a unique situation for the academy when a voice came from behind us.
"You’re having quite an interesting conversation, Louise."
The voice was that of a girl with distinctive red hair, exuding a provocative and intimidating tone.
The first thing that set her apart from Louise’s uniform was the red cape she wore.
Seeing Louise’s expression stiffen at the appearance of the red-haired girl, I guessed that she was someone Louise didn’t like.
"What’s wrong, Hayase-san?"
The girl, referred to as Hayase, ignored Louise and walked over to me.
She stopped within arm's reach and began observing me with keen interest.
It seemed she had carelessly entered my personal space, exposing herself defenselessly.
At the same time, it appeared she was confident in her own abilities, not considering me a threat.
Without even glancing at Louise, she began to explain why she approached me.
"I was curious about the rumored boy, so I thought I’d say hello. You don’t really seem like a boy for your age, though."
In front of the domineering girl, I must have had a puzzled expression, as Louise hurriedly introduced me.
"This is Hayase-san. She’s a real Valkyrie, but more than that, she’s the strongest person at the Third Academy."
"The strongest, you say?"
I understood that I had widened my eyes in surprise at the red-haired girl.
I certainly thought she was strong, but I hadn’t anticipated her being the strongest in the academy.
Feeling slighted, the red-haired girl looked up at me with a glare.
However, her expression quickly shifted to a provocative smile.
"To think you’d come to the academy, I thought you must be fearless, but it seems you’re just a fool who can’t even see the strength of your opponent."
If Louise said she was the strongest, then her abilities were surely formidable.
In my days as an infantryman, I could usually gauge someone’s strength with just a glance, but...
It seemed things wouldn’t work the same way here.
It would take me some time to discern the strength of a Valkyrie.
I straightened my posture and was about to apologize.
"I sincerely apologize for—"
"Hayase-san, we have plans now, so we’re leaving!"
I was abruptly pulled away as Louise clung to my left arm.
At that moment, she whispered in my ear.
"Actually, there’s a bit of history between Hayase-san and me, and if we get involved any further, it could cause trouble for you too, so let’s hurry and get out of here."
"I see."
Since it seemed there was some backstory between the two, I decided to follow Louise's lead, but—
"This sounds interesting, so I’ll join you. Is that okay, Louise?"
When I turned around, Hayase-san was wearing a meaningful smile.
In the awkward atmosphere, the three of us descended to the lower levels, with Louise leading the way, followed by me and Hayase-san in that order, as we progressed through the dimly lit corridor.
Having likely passed through here many times, Louise moved without hesitation.
She turned right and left, passing through several intersections.
If someone didn’t know better, they might truly feel like they had wandered into a maze.
Occasionally, the flickering fluorescent lights made it seem like the corridor wasn’t well maintained.
It was doubtful whether cleaning was done even once a year.
Hayase-san, who was following behind me, remained silent, making it hard to gauge her thoughts.
Whenever I glanced back, she seemed overly cautious of our surroundings.
While I had shown confidence above ground, she now radiated tension upon entering the basement, which concerned me.
As I debated whether to say something, Louise, unable to endure the atmosphere any longer, spoke up.
"Once we get through here, we’ll reach a spot where you can see the outside! It’s like a balcony, and the atmosphere is nice. It’s my favorite place!"
Determined to change the mood, Louise’s enthusiasm prompted me to lend my support.
"That sounds like a wonderful place!"
However, Hayase-san seemed uninterested.
"There are plenty of similar places above ground, so why come all the way down here? I really dislike dark and damp places like this."
If that’s the case, why did she even come along? The question almost slipped out.
Louise couldn’t hold back her frustration at Hayase-san’s dismissive comment.
With a sudden shift from her earlier timid demeanor, she turned around and approached Hayase-san.
They stood close enough to reach each other, so I halted my steps as well.
"It was you who decided to tag along, Hayase-san, right? If you don’t like it, you can go back."
Faced with Louise’s glare, Hayase-san wore a defiant smile.
"I was just worried you might do something inappropriate with the boy."
I quickly grasped what Hayase-san was concerned about.
She seemed to worry that a romantic relationship was developing between me and Louise.
If I didn’t clear up this misunderstanding, it would only cause trouble for Louise.
"No, that’s not it. Louise is just showing me around because I’m unfamiliar with the academy. There’s nothing for you to worry about, Hayase-san."
Hayase-san shot me a look that was hard to interpret.
"You’re the one misunderstanding. What I meant was—"
Before Hayase-san could finish, I looked up at the ceiling.
I sensed three presences approaching from the large duct, and my body reacted instinctively to the ominous aura.
"Excuse me!"
As I dashed forward, I grabbed both Louise and Hayase-san and continued running.
Louise began to squirm in my right arm.
"Hey, what are you doing all of a sudden!! Koshon!"
Louise’s tone was more forceful than usual, but it was understandable that she would be upset after being suddenly swept up.
"I’ll take the punishment later! We need to get out of here quickly!"
I had no confidence in being able to escape while carrying both of them.
While being held by me, Hayase-san was watching the duct above.
"Tch."
Just after Hayase-san clicked her tongue, gunfire erupted from the duct.
The sound of gunfire was suppressed, but multiple bullets struck the floor.
Seeing this, Louise quickly deduced what was being used.
"A silencer!?"
"It seems so."
After firing several rounds through the duct, the attackers kicked open the duct cover and dropped down.
They wore black rider suits and helmets.
The visors were down, obscuring their expressions, but the tight-fitting suits indicated that all three attackers were women.
One of them held a silenced pistol, while the other two wielded knives.
It seemed they had cameras hidden behind the visors, as small, round lights flickered ominously in the dim corridor.
It was unclear whether they had night vision or recording capabilities, but there was no doubt that a significant amount of money had been spent on their equipment.
The leader, who seemed to be in charge, issued commands to her companions in a voice that was unrecognizable, likely due to a voice changer.
"Don’t kill the two girls; just hurt them a bit. I’ll take care of the boy."
Calmly, as if performing a task, she aimed her pistol at me.
Fortunately, there was a side passage, so I dove into it, releasing the two girls and pushing them forward.
Following behind them, we navigated the maze-like lower corridors.
While Louise was concerned about what was happening behind us, she remained surprisingly calm.
She began to analyze the attackers with a cool head.
"It’s impossible to be attacked in a place like this. We decided to come here just moments ago. Plus, with that kind of equipment... they’re too well-prepared."
Louise was clearly troubled by the current situation.
As she organized her thoughts, Hayase-san shot her a sharp glance, maintaining a speed that showed no sign of breathlessness.
"You’re remarkably calm. I thought you’d be a bit more flustered."
"If I panicked over something like this, I wouldn’t be able to become a Valkyrie."
Hayase-san had no retort to Louise’s response.
Is this what it means to be a Valkyrie? Both of them quickly regained their composure, having trained for situations like this.
While Hayase-san showed little change, she wasn’t shaken at all.
Louise, on the other hand, seemed a bit tense; the gentle demeanor she had earlier had vanished.
Now, with a sharp focus on analyzing the enemy’s information, Louise exuded the same presence as a soldier heading into battle.
I had thought it would be a disaster if things escalated, but with this, we should be fine.
As I fled from the attackers, I half-convinced myself that I was the target based on the enemy’s earlier statement.
Since they mentioned handling me, it was unlikely they had mistakenly attacked.
While I kept an eye on our pursuers, I recalled the words of Principal Kase.
He had said that many people did not take kindly to my presence.
The attackers were definitely targeting me.
I turned my gaze to the two girls and proposed, "It seems they’re after me, so let’s split up to retreat. I’ll draw the enemies away, so you two should hurry to the surface."
Hayase-san turned to me, replacing the flustered Louise.
"You want us to use you as bait to escape? No way. Besides, those guys are probably Valkyries or their rejects."
I didn’t know much about the rejects, but there was no time to confirm that.
"Even so, this is the best option we have right now."
The three attackers were closing in behind us.
As one of them drew their pistol while running, I turned to look back and swung my right arm sideways.
The sleeve of my clothing tore, and a bullet lodged itself in my right arm.
"Ugh!"
It hurt, but it hadn’t penetrated.
Louise’s eyes widened as she stared at my right arm, but that wasn’t my priority right now.
My right arm, created from Gijuu cells, had superior physical strength.
Given the small caliber of the bullets they were using, I could easily fight back by using my arm as a shield.
The attackers seemed slightly surprised that their bullets had only grazed me.
I sensed the leader smirking slightly.
"You’re a monster too, huh? I can’t just let you go."
With my right arm positioned as a shield, I contemplated how to get through this situation.
What should I do to survive... Before I could find an answer, Louise spoke up behind me.
"Thank you?"
What language was that? Just as I thought so, the leader casually replied.
"Rukel Panstu K Suwa?"
When I remembered it was French, the leader pulled the trigger.
As shots rang out one after another, I used my right arm to block the bullets.
There wasn’t much time left.
"I’ll handle these guys! While I do, you two get to the surface and call for help!"
Since I was facing away from them, I couldn’t see their expressions, but it seemed Louise would follow my judgment.
"I’ll go get help right away!"
I heard the sound of footsteps retreating.
The leader issued commands to her subordinates.
"We don’t have time for help to arrive. Subdue them."
The two subordinates charged at me with knives drawn.
In order to buy time for Louise and Hayase-san to escape, I tried to block them, but something red zipped past me.
By the time I realized it was Hayase-san, she had delivered a knee strike to the head of the attacker with the knife.
Not only was her speed impressive, but her physical abilities were astonishing, causing my brain to momentarily spiral into confusion at the impossible sight.
Since Hayase-san had jumped out, Louise also came to a halt.
"Hayase-san!?"
Ignoring Louise’s admonition, Hayase-san pressed the attack against the enemy in front of her.
Even though I had told them to run, the Valkyrie had jumped in first.
I was bewildered, but my long experience on the battlefield told me that the moment you hesitate is the most dangerous.
Instinctively, I turned my gaze to the other attacker and charged at them.
I positioned myself to block the leader from using her pistol by standing in front of her subordinate.
The attacker, seemingly irritated, shouted, "Get out of the way!"
"I won’t let you."
I dodged the knife thrust aimed at me and quickly grabbed the attacker’s arm to apply a joint lock, intending to break it... but I couldn’t manage it.
I should have been able to break an adult male’s arm, but I only managed to injure the joint.
"Ugh!?" the attacker groaned in pain, and as she forcefully pulled away from me, she dropped her knife.
The leader, who seemed to be in charge of the attackers, returned her silenced pistol to its holster.
"I’ll handle this one. You take care of your comrade."
She directed her subordinate, who was struggling against Hayase-san, to assist her.
"R-Right."
As the leader picked up the knife that her subordinate had dropped, she closed the distance between us.
I broke into a cold sweat at the leader’s speed.
"She’s fast!?"
The fight had turned into close combat, but the leader’s movements were superior to those of the subordinate I had just faced.
She seemed skilled in combat techniques using a knife, leaving no openings to grab her arm and break it.
"What’s wrong? Isn’t close combat your specialty?"
Claiming to know me, the leader avoided my strikes and knife attacks while maintaining her focus.
"Are you targeting me? Who are you people?"
Given that they had a voice changer and seemed to enjoy conversing, I held out a faint hope that she might answer my question.
Or perhaps, if I could distract her even slightly with conversation, it would be a win.
The leader jumped back to create distance and pretended to think before responding.
She didn’t seem rushed to eliminate me, which could have been a sign of confidence.
"I’d say we’re fallen angels."
"Fallen angels?"
As I repeated her words, Louise took over the conversation in my stead.
"I see... So you were once a Valkyrie. If you’re from the Third Academy, does that make you a senior?"
It seemed Louise interpreted the fallen angels as former Valkyries who had fallen from grace.
And it appeared that her interpretation wasn’t entirely incorrect.
"I don’t intend to say much more."
That was clever.
I lacked the confidence to continue a conversation with the enemy.
Seeing Louise trying to extract information from the leader brought me some relief, as it meant she had regained her composure.
I wished she would go above ground and call for help, but...
After glancing at Hayase-san, the leader’s voice turned cold as she surveyed her struggling subordinates.
"Well, it seems we don’t have much time left. Let’s take care of this."
From the corner of my eye, I noticed Hayase-san effortlessly handling the two attackers.
The leader remained calm, not showing any signs of panic despite the situation becoming unfavorable.
Even though the odds were turning against them, she didn’t seem to regard it as a problem.
A chill ran down my spine at her eerie demeanor, and just then, I raised my right arm to guard against an incoming strike.
The leader’s heel drop came crashing down with an impact that was beyond what I would expect from a human.
I couldn’t hide my surprise at the sheer force of the blow.
I had been focused on the knife she held, but each strike she delivered was a dangerous attack that could inflict fatal damage.
The leader, noticing my moment of hesitation, spoke in a voice devoid of emotion, unlike before.
"Heavy, isn’t it? Consider it a parting gift. I’ll make sure you savor it."
Even if I was a strong soldier, I wouldn’t be able to replicate the same level of movement and power as the attackers.
My mind was in turmoil, unable to believe that the woman in front of me had just delivered that attack.
The instincts I had honed during my infantry days were now hindering me.
I leaped back, using my right arm as a shield to deflect her attack.
As I blocked her punch, a knee strike aimed at my abdomen followed immediately.
I caught it with my left hand and used the momentum to leap backward.
I could tell this opponent was experienced. That was the impression I had of her.
In the narrow corridor, she skillfully unleashed a spinning kick, which I blocked with my right arm, and I could almost hear her laughing through the voice changer.
"If you were an ordinary human, you’d be broken or torn apart. Indeed, that special right arm is something else."
It was clear that classified information had been leaked.
If it had leaked, from where? No, more importantly, I had more questions to ask the attackers in front of me.
"I have some questions for you."
Noticing the shift in my demeanor, the leader began to chuckle.
"Not running away? Just barking, you mere human."
"Sorry, but I’m no longer human."
Kicking off the floor with my left foot, regenerated from Gijuu cells, I managed to surprise the leader slightly and delay her reaction.
It was a sign that she had been overly focused on my right arm, but she also seemed experienced enough to respond quickly.
My regenerated heart was pounding rapidly, accompanied by pain.
I felt a throbbing sensation and pain in my left eye.
In exchange, I gained the reaction speed to move after observing my opponent’s actions.
This was a trump card I would never normally use.
No, it was a forbidden technique I shouldn’t use.
For a short time, activating the Gijuu cells would enhance my physical abilities, but the strain on my body was too great, making it prohibited.
"Too slow!"
The leader was taken aback by my accelerated reaction speed.
As I struck my left fist into her abdomen, I felt something hard beneath her rider suit.
The sensation was different from hitting flesh.
What I had thought was just a rider suit turned out to be a rather sophisticated armor.
As the leader jumped back, she glanced at her fallen subordinates.
The two attackers lay sprawled on the floor.
Having finished off the two, Hayase-san seemed to have the upper hand, taunting the leader.
"You seem to be in a different league. Next, you’ll face me."
Her stance, stepping on the defeated attackers while provoking the leader, was quite brazen.
The leader turned her gaze back to me.
"…You should be careful from now on. There are many who dislike your presence here."
With that, the leader skillfully pulled out a stun grenade.
Louise immediately closed her eyes and covered her ears, but Hayase-san couldn’t see from her position.
If things turned around, the maximum combat strength, Hayase-san, would be put in danger with her senses blocked.
If the situation reversed, the attackers would likely accomplish their objective.
My body moved instinctively.
Seeing me jump on top of Hayase-san to shield her, the leader was smiling.
"I don’t dislike that decision."
I leaped onto Hayase-san, wrapping my arms around her head to shield her eyes from the dazzling flash.
At first, Hayase-san looked surprised and resisted slightly, but she quickly seemed to understand my intent.
I couldn’t protect my own ears, and the shock distorted my face.
The pain in my ears and the strain on my body reached their limits, rendering me unable to move.
Before I knew it, the attackers had gathered their comrades and fled.
The immediate danger seemed to have passed.
As my consciousness faded, I saw Hayase-san crawl out from my arms and immediately start arguing with Louise.
I couldn’t hear what they were saying, but I had reached my limit.
The toll of the short-term enhancement of my physical abilities was far too heavy to be useful.
I had considered several times whether it could be useful as a pilot, but being unable to move afterward was out of the question.
However, seeing the two of them safe brought me a sense of joy, knowing that even an unusable trump card had served its purpose.
As everyone left the classroom, Louise brought her hands together and apologized to me.
"I'm really sorry! I never thought everyone would get that angry."
"I don't mind. Besides, the experimental unit is still being adjusted outside the academy, so it hasn't been brought in yet. There's nothing to see."
"Is that so? Then, what are you doing, Ren-kun?"
"I'm attending lectures and training. Well then, I have to go."
Checking my watch, I realized it was almost time for the lecture to start.
If I didn't hurry to the hangar, I wouldn't make it in time.
I left the classroom at a brisk pace, and I could hear Louise's cheerful voice behind me.
"See you tomorrow!"
Stopping at the entrance of the classroom, I turned around to salute her—then clenched my right hand tightly.
I gave a small wave with my right hand.
"Yes. Well then, see you tomorrow."
